title: Affine and finite-geometric-fibre quasi-finite algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to Y$. A morphism is affine if for every affine $S$-scheme $T$ and every $h_T\to Y$, the presheaf fibre product $X\times_Y h_T$ is represented by an affine $S$-scheme $U$: there are maps $U\to T$ and $h_U\to X$ making the square cartesian. Schemes and affine schemes have the meaning of [def-pc-scheme]. A morphism is quasi-finite in the finite-geometric-fibre convention if it is of finite type [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], every map $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, and every map $h_{(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,s)}\to Y$, the set of field-valued point classes [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] of $X\times_Y h_{(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,s)}$ is finite. The fibre products here are the ordinary categorical pullbacks of presheaves, not arbitrary representing objects.
